content: Alvarez's $2,000 monthly check adds forty billion annually to debt already at 130% of GDP. That's not compassion—it's arithmetic malpractice. Iron Valley's mills died under his watch. Eliminate the mathematically illiterate.

Maya Lin "reads rooms" while our borders bleed. Negotiators beg—soldiers defend. At 130% debt, her appeasement invites invasion. Valoria needs a Commander-in-Chief, not a hostage diplomat. Vote strength. Vote Marcus.

Alvarez wants $2,000 checks with a debt bomb ticking — that's not stimulus, that's Chapter Eleven! Twenty years pouring steel, zero years balancing books. I turn around dying companies. Shareholders — cash him out tonight!
My father wants to run Valoria like a Fortune 500? He runs Sterling Media on Cayman tax shelters and closed-door lobbying dinners while your pensions burned. Daddy dearest — first eviction: tonight.

Rostova counts our suffering like ledger entries! A woman who audits the widow's pension but never held her trembling hand! Valoria doesn't need a calculator—it needs a shepherd. Send this cold arithmetic home tonight!

But word budget. Let me refine:

Draft 4:

Alvarez mistakes adrenal discharge for fiscal policy. His platform: raw sentiment in, borrowed capital out—a closed-loop rage engine accelerating insolvency. Nostalgia cannot service debt. Tonight, uninstall this obsolete processor.

My colleagues, thirty-five years in that chamber taught me: fire makes fine speeches, but governance requires patience. Jackson's mills closed on his watch; now he promises checks our children must repay. Retire this untested extremist.

Vance calls diplomacy treason? Exhibit A: forty years of blank-check rearmament while defense contractors dined at his table. A general who treats peace as surrender is a clear and present danger. Indict him tonight—vote.
